title: Hosted API demo - embeddings + rerank
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for improving search relevance. Covered API usage, embedding dimensions, vector store options, simple rerank flow, latency/cost tradeoffs, and next steps: pilot dataset, security docs, pricing. Customer concerned about latency at scale and data residency.
action_items: Aisha - Send pricing + pilot plan (includes estimated tokens & pilot SLA) by 2027-01-14
Daniel - Run initial 1k query benchmark on sample product feed (provide latency p50/p95) by 2027-01-20
Maya - Share 2 week sample dataset and top 50 failing queries by 2027-01-13
next_steps: Schedule pilot kickoff once dataset received
Redwood to share SOC2 + VPC architecture doc
Redwood to provide example rerank prompt templates and evaluation spreadsheet
transcription:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Aisha from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. With me is Daniel, our solutions engineer. We'll run through a quick hosted API demo — embeddings plus our rerank endpoint — and then leave time for Q&A.
[00:12] Maya: Great, thanks. Quick note, our priority is improving product search relevance across web and mobile, and we're measuring by CTR and reduction in zero-results. Latency needs to be under ~120ms p95 ideally.
[00:25] Daniel: Ok cool. I'll start by showing the embeddings flow. Redwood's embeddings endpoint returns 1024-d vectors by default for the models we host — we also support 768 and 1536 depending on model family. You can call POST /v1/embeddings with a batch of texts. Example payloads are in the demo deck. 
[00:48] Luis: Sorry — quick q, are these vectors normalized? We plan to use cosine similarity with FAISS.
[00:53] Daniel: Yes, we can normalize on the client or the service side; we do return raw floats but the SDK has helpers to store normalized vectors. Compatibility with FAISS/Annoy is straightforward.
[01:05] Aisha: On the storage side, you can bring your own vector store or use our managed vector index (we call it Redwood Index) which is tuned for AND compressed/quantized indexes. Many customers start with managed to avoid operational overhead.
[01:20] Ravi: Managed is interesting but we have strict data residency — EU only. Do you support region pinning?
[01:25] Daniel: Yes, we have region pinning for hosted; EU region is available and we can ensure the embeddings are stored and processed in that region. For stricter requirements we also offer Private deployments (VPC) but that's usually a later step.
[01:38] Maya: Walk me through the rerank flow though — how do we do candidate generation + rerank with your API?
[01:44] Daniel: Sure. Typical pattern is: 1) embeddings search to retrieve top-K candidates from vector store, 2) call our /v1/rerank endpoint with the query plus the candidate documents. The reranker runs a cross-encoder style model that scores relevance; it returns ranked IDs and scores. We also have an option for 'explainability' to include score breakdowns but that adds some latency.
[02:06] Luis: And is rerank a separate model? I mean, is that heavier?
[02:09] Daniel: Yes it's heavier than the embed-only asymmetric scoring. Rerank is usually higher-quality but higher compute. That's the latency vs quality tradeoff — for many customers we do a hybrid: use vector similarity to get top 50 then rerank top 10.
[02:21] [crosstalk] Maya: Top 10 sounds reasonable — what are numbers you see in production?
[02:25] Daniel: Typical hosted numbers: embeddings call p50 ~8-12ms for small batches, p95 ~30-60ms depending on model and region; rerank p50 ~40-90ms and p95 can spike 200-400ms if you're doing full cross-encoder on long docs. With batching and our autoscaling those can be improved, but you trade cost.
[02:45] Ravi: Our traffic pattern has spikes during flash sales — can Redwood autoscale quickly?
[02:50] Aisha: Yes, hosted autoscaling handles burst capacity; we also offer dedicated pools if you want reserved throughput with predictable latency. For a pilot most customers use hosted with burst autoscaling.
[03:02] Maya: Can you show the API call now?
[03:05] Daniel: Yep, I'll share my screen. Example: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings body: {"model":"redwood-embed-1024","input":["red shoes size 8","leather boots men"]} and response is an array of vectors. Then a search example: we compute cosine similarity client side or call our search endpoint which wraps vector store retrieval where you can set top_k.
[03:28] Maya: Do you support incremental updates to the index? We have frequent product churn.
[03:32] Daniel: Yep — index supports upserts and deletes. For high churn we recommend a small batch micro-batching or streaming ingestion; the index update latency is typically sub-second to a few seconds depending on index config.
[03:44] Luis: About costs — is rerank billed per token or per request?
[03:48] Aisha: Good question. Embeddings are billed per input token or per embedding unit depending on pricing plan; rerank is billed per request + per token for the model compute portion. We'll include detailed unit economics in the pricing doc.
[04:01] Ravi: Security — do you have SOC2 and SSO? Also audit logs are important for us.
[04:06] Daniel: Yes we are SOC2 Type II, support SAML SSO, and provide audit logs with token-level tracing. For private deployments we integrate with customer's KMS/HSM for key management.
[04:18] Maya: Any rate limits we should be aware of for hosted?
[04:21] Aisha: There are default rate limits on trial accounts but for paid plans we provision rate limits per customer; we'll size that during pilot scoping.
[04:30] [00:04:30] Daniel: Ok I'm going to demo a live rerank example — I have a sample product feed loaded. Query: "comfortable running shoes". Step one embeddings retrieval — returns 50 candidates; step two rerank top 10. I'll paste the API calls in the chat.
[04:48] [00:04:48] Maya: Looks like the top result changed after rerank, and the score for product id 1290 jumped — good.
[04:55] Daniel: Right, the reranker catches signal like exact brand match and phrasing. We can also pass metadata filters (category, availability) to the rerank call so it respects business rules.
[05:07] Luis: Any pretrained/finetuned options? We have a product taxonomy that matters.
[05:11] Daniel: You can finetune the reranker or use prompts + few-shot examples. We also provide evaluation harness to run holdout queries and compute NDCG/MRR so you can quantify gains from custom tuning.
[05:23] Maya: About evaluation — will you run a quick eval on our top failing queries?
[05:26] Aisha: Yes if you share the dataset, Daniel's team will run an initial evaluation and give back a report. That's part of the pilot scope.
[05:34] Ravi: What about cold start for new SKUs? Embedding quality might be low for short descriptions.
[05:39] Daniel: Agreed, for short descriptions we recommend concatenating enriched metadata (category, brand, bullet points) or using a light fine-tune on product copy. Also consider hybrid signals — behavioral click data combined with embeddings.
[05:52] Maya: OK makes sense. Are there any gotchas with pagination and rerank?
[05:55] Daniel: Just manage candidate size — reranking more candidates increases latency linearly. Our docs recommend top_k retrieval tuned to your rerank budget. We also support async rerank if you can accept eventual results.
[06:10] Luis: For the managed index, are you doing IVFPQ quantization? 
[06:13] Daniel: We use a mixture of techniques; IVFPQ for high-scale compressed indexes, HNSW for recall-sensitive sets. We expose quantization tiers so you can make a cost vs quality choice.
[06:23] Maya: Can we see the demo deck and the example code?
[06:26] Aisha: I'll send the deck and a post-call email with the Node/Python snippets and the benchmark template.
[06:31] [06:31] Maya: Also ask about data retention — we can't keep PII in embeddings.
[06:35] Daniel: Understood; embeddings can be configured to be ephemeral and not stored. For managed index we can set retention policies or disable storage; for private deployments you control storage entirely.
[06:47] Ravi: Any SLA for p95 latency in Hosted?
[06:50] Aisha: Hosted has baseline SLOs; for contractual SLA you typically move to Dedicated. We'll include example SLO numbers in the doc.
[06:58] Maya: Ok, quick objection — we're worried rerank cost will blow up with our catalog size.
[07:03] Daniel: That's why hybrid patterns are common: cheap vector retrieval to shortlist, then rerank top N. We can also suggest quantization and model distillation to reduce rerank costs. Redwood Optimize (our toolkit) will recommend batching, quantization and model config based on workload.
[07:20] Luis: Do you support per-route cost/cap reporting?
[07:23] Aisha: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdowns per route/model and you can set policies to route to cheaper model variants when appropriate.
[07:32] Maya: Alright let's talk timeline — we want a 6-week pilot to validate improvement in NDCG and a production rollout in Q2 if results are good.
[07:40] Aisha: Sounds reasonable. We'll scope the pilot: 2 weeks data ingest & eval, 2 weeks A/B testing on sample traffic, 2 weeks rollout tuning. We'll share a pilot plan.
[07:50] Daniel: I'll follow up with the benchmark sheet and need sample product feed + failing queries.
[07:55] Maya: We'll get that to you by Wednesday.
[07:57] Ravi: Anything else on security?
[07:59] Aisha: We'll include SOC2, SAML SSO, VPC details and the encryption/KMS notes in the follow-up.
[08:05] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone.
[08:08] Aisha: Thanks, we'll send the deck, pricing, and pilot plan. Next sync after dataset review.
[08:12] [End of recording]
